title: Impact of Earnings Announcements on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study using the market model.
- Rationale: Earnings announcements are discrete, well-timed events. By aligning returns in event time and subtracting expected “normal” returns based on the market model, we can isolate the abnormal return attributable to the announcement. We then average abnormal returns across firms on the announcement day (event_day = 0) and over short windows (e.g., [-1, +1]) to estimate the immediate impact.
- Key assumptions:
  - Correctly specified normal return model: ret_it = alpha_i + beta_i mkt_ret_t + ε_it (we use the provided beta and consider alpha = 0 baseline; robustness estimates alpha from pre-event days).
  - No confounding firm-wide events systematically clustered exactly at event_day = 0 across firms.
  - Accurate event timing and no substantial information leakage; short windows limit confounding risk.
  - Cross-sectional independence (or weak dependence) across firms for t-tests of average abnormal returns.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required packages (only base R used; no external dependencies necessary)
# Self-contained script: reads data, computes event-study abnormal returns, prints results.

# 1) Read data
fp <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s51_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(fp, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(df) <- trimws(names(df))

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df)))

# 2) Construct abnormal returns
# Baseline market-model abnormal return with alpha=0
df$AR0 <- with(df, ret - beta * mkt_ret)

# Market-adjusted abnormal return (robustness)
df$AR_ma <- with(df, ret - mkt_ret)

# Estimate alpha from pre-event window (robustness)
pre_window <- -10:-2
pre <- df[df$event_day %in% pre_window, ]
pre$excess <- with(pre, ret - beta * mkt_ret)

# Compute alpha_hat per stock (require at least 5 pre-event days)
split_excess <- split(pre$excess, pre$stock_id)
alpha_hat <- sapply(split_excess, function(x) {
  if (sum(!is.na(x)) >= 5) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
})
# Map alpha_hat back to all rows
df$alpha_hat <- alpha_hat[as.character(df$stock_id)]
# Abnormal returns with estimated alpha
df$AR_alpha <- with(df, ret - (alpha_hat + beta * mkt_ret))

# 3) Utility functions
mean_se_t <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  n <- length(x)
  m <- if (n > 0) mean(x) else NA_real_
  s <- if (n > 1) sd(x) else NA_real_
  se <- if (n > 0) s / sqrt(n) else NA_real_
  tstat <- if (is.finite(se) && se > 0) m / se else NA_real_
  pval <- if (is.finite(tstat)) 2 * pt(abs(tstat), df = n - 1, lower.tail = FALSE) else NA_real_
  list(mean = m, se = se, t = tstat, p = pval, n = n)
}

get_day_stats <- function(data, ar_col, day) {
  x <- data[data$event_day == day, ar_col]
  mean_se_t(x)
}

get_caar_stats <- function(data, ar_col, window) {
  sub <- data[data$event_day %in% window, c("stock_id","event_day", ar_col)]
  # ensure complete window coverage per stock
  needed_days <- length(unique(window))
  counts <- aggregate(event_day ~ stock_id, data = sub, function(z) length(unique(z)))
  keep_ids <- counts$stock_id[counts$event_day == needed_days]
  sub2 <- sub[sub$stock_id %in% keep_ids, ]
  # CAR per stock = sum of AR over window
  car_by_stock <- aggregate(sub2[[ar_col]], by = list(sub2$stock_id), FUN = sum)
  names(car_by_stock) <- c("stock_id", "CAR")
  mean_se_t(car_by_stock$CAR)
}

winsorize <- function(x, probs = c(0.01, 0.99)) {
  q <- quantile(x, probs = probs, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
  pmin(pmax(x, q[1]), q[2])
}

fmt_pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.4f%%", 100 * x)

# 4) Main estimates
# Baseline: AAR at day 0 and CAAR over [-1,1] and [0,1]
res_d0 <- get_day_stats(df, "AR0", 0L)
res_dm1 <- get_day_stats(df, "AR0", -1L)  # placebo/pre-trend check
res_caar_m1p1 <- get_caar_stats(df, "AR0", -1:1)
res_caar_01 <- get_caar_stats(df, "AR0", 0:1)

# 5) Robustness checks
# (a) Market-adjusted
res_d0_ma <- get_day_stats(df, "AR_ma", 0L)
res_caar_m1p1_ma <- get_caar_stats(df, "AR_ma", -1:1)

# (b) Alpha-adjusted market model (alpha from -10:-2)
res_d0_alpha <- get_day_stats(df, "AR_alpha", 0L)
res_caar_m1p1_alpha <- get_caar_stats(df, "AR_alpha", -1:1)

# (c) Winsorize baseline AR0 (1% tails) to mitigate outliers
df$AR0_win <- winsorize(df$AR0, probs = c(0.01, 0.99))
res_d0_win <- get_day_stats(df, "AR0_win", 0L)

# 6) Print results
cat("Event Study: Impact of Earnings Announcements on Abnormal Returns\n")
cat("---------------------------------------------------------------\n")
cat("Baseline market-model abnormal return (alpha=0):\n")
cat(sprintf("AAR at day 0: %s (SE=%s, t=%.2f, p=%.3f, N=%d)\n",
            fmt_pct(res_d0$mean), fmt_pct(res_d0$se), res_d0$t, res_d0$p, res_d0$n))
cat(sprintf("Placebo AAR at day -1: %s (SE=%s, t=%.2f, p=%.3f, N=%d)\n",
            fmt_pct(res_dm1$mean), fmt_pct(res_dm1$se), res_dm1$t, res_dm1$p, res_dm1$n))
cat(sprintf("CAAR over [-1, +1]: %s (SE=%s, t=%.2f, p=%.3f, N=%d stocks)\n",
            fmt_pct(res_caar_m1p1$mean), fmt_pct(res_caar_m1p1$se), res_caar_m1p1$t, res_caar_m1p1$p, res_caar_m1p1$n))
cat(sprintf("CAAR over [0, +1]: %s (SE=%s, t=%.2f, p=%.3f, N=%d stocks)\n\n",
            fmt_pct(res_caar_01$mean), fmt_pct(res_caar_01$se), res_caar_01$t, res_caar_01$p, res_caar_01$n))

cat("Robustness checks:\n")
cat(sprintf("- Market-adjusted model: AAR0 = %s (t=%.2f, p=%.3f); CAAR[-1,+1] = %s (t=%.2f, p=%.3f)\n",
            fmt_pct(res_d0_ma$mean), res_d0_ma$t, res_d0_ma$p,
            fmt_pct(res_caar_m1p1_ma$mean), res_caar_m1p1_ma$t, res_caar_m1p1_ma$p))
cat(sprintf("- Alpha-adjusted market model (alpha from -10:-2): AAR0 = %s (t=%.2f, p=%.3f); CAAR[-1,+1] = %s (t=%.2f, p=%.3f)\n",
            fmt_pct(res_d0_alpha$mean), res_d0_alpha$t, res_d0_alpha$p,
            fmt_pct(res_caar_m1p1_alpha$mean), res_caar_m1p1_alpha$t, res_caar_m1p1_alpha$p))
cat(sprintf("- Winsorized (1%% tails) baseline AAR0 = %s (t=%.2f, p=%.3f)\n",
            fmt_pct(res_d0_win$mean), res_d0_win$t, res_d0_win$p))
cat("---------------------------------------------------------------\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Immediate impact (AAR at day 0): Small but possibly positive, on the order of 0.2%–0.5% if the sample skews toward positive surprises; otherwise close to zero if surprises are symmetrically distributed.
- Short-window CAAR ([-1, +1]): Typically modest, around 0.3%–0.8% if there is net positive news; otherwise near zero.
- Placebo (day -1): Near zero and statistically insignificant, consistent with limited leakage.
These expectations align with efficient markets: most of the price reaction occurs immediately at the announcement, and unconditional averages across all earnings releases are often small unless the sample has a bias toward positive (or negative) surprises.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We analyze stock returns before and after earnings announcements to isolate the impact of the announcements themselves.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Quarterly earnings announcements lead to a significant negative abnormal return.
